title: Only the designated Crafter may commit code to a Spell, and only suggestions authored by a designated Reviewer
content:
A.1.10.2.4.7.2.3 states that "the designated Crafter is the only person or entity permitted to commit GitHub code suggestions to the Spell. The Crafter can only commit suggestions that have been made by a designated Reviewer for the particular Spell. However, using GitHub suggestions is generally discouraged while developing the Spell."

Two constraints compose here. Single-writer: every byte in the Spell passes through one accountable party, so there is no path by which code enters without the Crafter having seen and accepted it. Closed set of proposers: even suggestions must originate from a designated Reviewer, so an outside participant cannot get code into the pull request by offering a helpful one-click fix.

The reason this needs saying is that GitHub's suggestion feature is a genuine authority leak. It lets a commenter write code that a maintainer commits with a single click, under the maintainer's name, often without reading it as carefully as a hand-typed change. That collapses the author/reviewer separation the rest of the process is built on.

Discouraging the feature outright — even for authorized Reviewers — reflects the same reasoning as "Attention to Detail" (A.1.10.2.4.7.4.2), which requires code to be handled line by line. A one-click accept is precisely the interaction that bypasses line-by-line attention, so convenience is treated as the hazard rather than the benefit.
description: A.1.10.2.4.7.2.3 gives the Spell exactly one writer so review cannot inject code; GitHub's suggestion feature is permitted but discouraged even within that constraint.
